oneStopSecurity.note: Flughafen Zürich: depending on the country of origin, connecting passengers pass security again. Switzerland applies the EU aviation-security rules (EU–CH air transport agreement). EU one-stop security (Reg. 2015/1998 Attachment 4-B as amended by Reg. 2019/413 and 2025/920): passengers from EU / EEA / Swiss airports and from the recognised third countries are not re-screened on transfer. Ben Gurion (TLV) was removed by Reg. 2025/920, Kangerlussuaq, Guernsey, Isle of Man and Jersey too. Belgrade (BEG) was added by Reg. 2020/111 and not removed since (consolidated text reconstructed from mirrors, likely: docs/research/EVIDENCE_2026-11-02.md); Reg. 2025/920 applies from 21 May 2025. The official consolidated Attachment 4-B was not read (EUR-Lex: owner capture).

specialScreening.text: SWISS flights to the United States: "all travellers are required to be physically present at check-in due to document checks" (Zurich Airport SWISS page). This is a document check at check-in, not extra screening time: on a self-transfer, online check-in and the self bag drop are not enough; use a staffed desk. Whether connecting passengers with a through boarding pass have their documents checked at a transfer desk or the gate is not established.

deadline.text: El Al gate security must be finished 2 h before departure (El Al Switzerland page, search excerpt)

specialScreening.text: El Al at Zurich: check-in 2 (rows 3–4) opens 3 h before departure (airport page); El Al states that its gate security check must be finished 2 h before departure (search excerpt). Feed TLV departures use Dock E (E42, E57) and D (D25, D51): no dedicated area.

Flights to Israel: whether this airline has an additional document check, interview or separate screening at Zurich (only El Al is documented) is not established by any source we could read. Allow extra time and check with the airline.

US-bound flights: TSA / DHS enhanced security measures for all last-point-of-departure airports (2017, still the baseline as far as known) may add checks at check-in or at the gate (interviews, document checks, separate screening of electronics). The procedures are not public; no time is known.

lines.name: Skymetro (Airside Center ↔ Dock E)

ride.note: Two uncut front-window rides (2 s storyboards, two channels): departure → stop at the far platform 144 ± 4 s (dKFPf7433G0, 2023) and ≈130–138 s from first motion (-BrDR_bFtUU, Mar 2025); the bored-tunnel section takes 72 s and 70 s in the two videos. Independent check: doors closed ≈55 s → Dock E ≈185 s (Jnr5qlnvI1E, 2024, ≈130 s). Door-close → door-open ≈2.3–2.7 min; official 'around three minutes' kept as the max. All measurements predate the modernisation (a +14–20 s longer ride after it is reported only in unreadable search excerpts).

service.hours: Single tunnel (works phase 2): during Dock E flight operations (exact hours not published); relief buses at daily peaks
service.notes: Works phase 2 (announced 30 Oct 2026): from Tuesday 3 Nov 2026 the not yet modernised tunnel is closed for about six months, until about May 2027 (end date approximate; validUntil set to 31 May 2027). The official staff timetable of 27 Oct 2025 had planned phase 2 as 'Mo, 19. Oktober 2026: Sperrung Tunnel 1' with relief buses for 6 months until 'ca. Ende April 2027'; the later announcement (3 Nov 2026) is used, and the end stays 31 May 2027 (conservative). The Skymetro keeps running in the modernised tunnel with reduced capacity; a bus replacement service runs at the daily peaks (see l:zrh-skymetro-relief-bus, not routed). Hours and headway for phase 2 are not published, so no windows are set. Headway: one train shuttling in one tunnel gives a departure every full cycle ≈ 2 × (2.5 min ride + 1–2 min dwell) ≈ 7–9 min (derived); the official phase-1 single-shuttle headway of 6–7 min (three-car train, other tunnel) is consistent with this but is not assumed for phase 2.

service.hours: Single tunnel (works phase 1): Skymetro single shuttle with 3 cars 04:45–23:30, every 6–7 min (official diagram); buses 06:00–09:00 and 10:30–13:00
service.notes: Historical: tunnel 2 closed from Tue 4 Nov 2025 to about mid-June 2026 (official staff diagram 'Gültigkeit Bauphase 1: täglich 04.11.2025 – ca. Mitte Juni 2026'); one three-car train in tunnel 1 (cars labelled EU, EU, ICAO), 04:45–23:30, 'alle 6–7 min' (published, ev:zrh-p3-phase1-diagram). Buses carried part of the passengers 06:00–09:00 and 10:30–13:00. These figures belong to phase 1 only and are not carried over to phase 2.

service.hours: During Dock E flight operations (exact hours not published)
service.notes: Two-tunnel operation, one train per tunnel (dual shuttle). Applies before 4 Nov 2025, between the phases (mid-June – 2 Nov 2026: tunnel 1 with a three-car train, modernised tunnel 2 with a four-car train) and after the works (two four-car trains, from about May 2027). This is the service on 2026-10-31. Headway not published: platform countdowns showed 1:58 (2017) and ≈3:05 (2024) to the next train; two trains each cycling ≈7–9 min give a departure every ≈3.5–4.5 min per direction (derived).

lines.eligibility: Air passengers only (not public transport). Non-Schengen airside: departing passengers after exit passport control in the Airside Center, arriving and connecting passengers from Dock E. Passengers screened to EU standards and unscreened arrivals ride in separate cars (glass dividers on the platforms).
lines.notes: Cable-hauled air-cushion people mover, 1,138 m, two parallel tunnels under runway 10/28, max 47.9 km/h; ride 'around three minutes' (official), measured ≈2.2–2.5 min in motion. No intermediate stops. The line is never suspended by the 2025–27 modernisation (one tunnel always stays in service), so the works are modelled as dated service entries (single-tunnel headway), not as status periods. Capacity 8,000 → 10,000 passengers per hour and direction after the works (two four-car trains).

ride.note: No published or observed ride time; the apron route between the Airside Center side and Dock E is not documented.

Historical. Official staff diagram (27 Oct 2025): 'Busentlastung' 06:00–09:00 and 10:30–13:00, 'ca. alle 3 min'. Flows: 06:00–09:00 only ICAO passengers E → A/B; 10:30–13:00 ICAO E → A/B and EU A/B → E (ev:zrh-p3-phase1-diagram). ICAO/EU are read as the Skymetro car labels (unscreened non-EU-standard arrivals vs passengers screened to EU standard); stands, levels and the passport arrangement are not shown. Times 'können je nach Bedarf ... angepasst werden'.

Works phase 1 (tunnel 2 closed, daily 4 Nov 2025 – ca. mid-June 2026): peak-time buses 06:00–09:00 and 10:30–13:00, about every 3 min (official staff diagram).

Between the works phases both tunnels run; no relief buses. Phase 2 was planned for Mon 19 Oct 2026 in the official Oct 2025 timetable (later 'mid-October') and was then announced to start on 3 Nov 2026.
Works phase 2 (the not yet modernised tunnel closed for about six months, until about May 2027): bus replacement at the daily peaks.
After the works (two four-car trains); end date approximate ('May 2027').

A third-party map site claims the buses load at the B/D bus-gate level; not used (unreliable).

rules.text: Works phase 2 (official newsroom, 30 Oct 2026, read 2026-11-01): from 3 Nov 2026 the not yet renovated Skymetro tunnel is closed for about six months (until about May 2027); the Skymetro keeps running with reduced capacity in the renovated tunnel and replacement buses run only at the daily peaks ("zu Spitzenzeiten"). The release gives no bus hours and no passenger groups. The phase-1 bus hours (06:00–09:00 and 10:30–13:00, staff newsletter of 27 Oct 2025) are historical and are NOT applied to phase 2.

Dock A (gates A) serves Schengen flights only. Dock B serves both: each stand has a B number (Schengen) and a D number (non-Schengen) with separate passenger routes on two levels. Dock E (gates E) serves non-Schengen flights only. Lufthansa Group: Schengen flights from A and B, non-Schengen from D and E.

All departing passengers pass the central security check building (between Terminals 1/2 and the Airside Center; 26 checkpoints on four levels, single entrance from Terminal 1 or 2, in operation since 1 Dec 2011) and reach the common departure level of the Airside Center; non-Schengen passengers then pass exit passport control.

The passport control hall (underground, between Docks A and B, opened 2004, altered 2008–2011) links the Airside Center with Dock E and Dock B and is the hub for immigration, emigration and transfer between Schengen and non-Schengen areas. It is being expanded during operations from 2025 (full operation expected about 2030) with separate areas for immigration, emigration and transfer immigration and more e-gates.

Depending on the country of origin, connecting passengers pass security again (official transfer page). The Skymetro carries passengers screened to EU standards and unscreened arrivals in separate cars. Where the transfer security check is located is not established; it is not modelled as a control.
Arriving Schengen passengers leave through Arrival 1, non-Schengen passengers through Arrival 2 after entry passport control and customs.

The Skymetro is being modernised (four-car trains in dual-shuttle mode instead of three-car trains; new control and drive systems; plan approval 25 April 2024). Phase 1: tunnel 2 closed 4 Nov 2025 – about mid-June 2026, buses 06:00–09:00 and 10:30–13:00. Between the phases (so on 2026-10-31) both tunnels run. Phase 2: the not yet modernised tunnel closes from Tuesday 3 Nov 2026 for about six months (until about May 2027); the Skymetro keeps running in the modernised tunnel with reduced capacity and buses relieve the daily peaks. Earlier plans gave 19 Oct / 'mid-October' 2026 and 'end of April 2027'; the 30 Oct 2026 announcement supersedes them. Capacity 8,000 → 10,000 passengers per hour and direction.

Night curfew: no flight operations 23:00–06:00, with up to 30 min (to 23:30) for delayed departures and arrivals (in force since 29 July 2010). Slot coordination allocates no arrivals 23:00–06:09 and no departures 22:46–05:44. Terminal, security and Skymetro opening hours are not published, so night routes (23:30, 03:00) are computed as if the walks and the Skymetro were open and carry an 'hours not published' warning.

Dock A, its tower and the dock base will be replaced by a new Dock A built north of the current one (project start 2023, construction from 2027; dock base 'as of 2030'). The old Dock A stays in operation until the new dock is operational. As preparation, a temporary five-storey modular building south of Dock B (construction started May 2025, commissioning expected by 2027) will provide temporary bus gates, lounges and Airside Center logistics.

openQuestions.question: During Skymetro works phase 2 (3 Nov 2026 – about May 2027), at which hours and frequency do the relief buses run, which passenger flows are sent to them, where do they board (level; before or after exit passport control) and where do they arrive at Dock E? Phase 1 (official diagram): 06:00–09:00 and 10:30–13:00, about every 3 min; mornings ICAO E → A/B, midday also EU A/B → E; boarding points never published.
openQuestions.impact: The relief bus is drawn but not routed; at peaks the real route to Dock E may be a bus with a different time, and the Skymetro wait is a derived single-train value.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Owner capture of the official passenger notice for phase 2 (not on the renovation page as of 2026-10-31), or a dated photo/video of the bus signage in the passport control hall after 3 Nov 2026.

openQuestions.question: What are the Skymetro operating hours in normal and phase-2 service (phase 1 single shuttle: 04:45–23:30 every 6–7 min, official; does normal service also stop during the curfew?) and headway (normal and during the single-tunnel works), and the night opening hours of the central security check and the passport control hall?
openQuestions.impact: Wait times are derived from countdown displays and the train cycle; at 23:30 and 03:00 every route is computed as if open and carries an 'hours not published' warning.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Ask Flughafen Zürich, or time two consecutive departures and note the first/last train on site; owner capture of the BAZL plan-approval documents (the PDFs return 404) and of the 2005-style official transfer-time brochure (routesonline copy HTTP 403).

openQuestions.question: Where do connecting passengers from airports outside EU one-stop security pass the transfer security check (Airside Center Skymetro arrival level, passport control hall, Dock E)?
openQuestions.impact: Transfers from such origins may need an extra 5–30 min not included in the matrix.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Owner capture of the interactive map (LocusLabs) layers, or a 2025–2026 walkthrough from a non-EU-OSS origin.

openQuestions.question: Do D-gate passengers clear passport control in the central hall below the Airside Center or in a separate control on the lower level of Dock B?
openQuestions.impact: Affects the B ↔ D transfer time and the D arrivals flow; currently both go through the central hall node.
openQuestions.howToResolve: A dated walkthrough from the Airside Center to a D gate, or the official interactive map.

openQuestions.question: Are A01–A06 and A50–A59 both current bus-gate ranges (OSM: 'Busgate A (A50-59)', formerly A01–A10), and are D51–D58, E18–E19 and E62–E67 bus gates?
openQuestions.impact: Bus flags and gate placement may be wrong for these groups.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Official departure board snapshots for these gates, or photos of the bus-gate signage.

openQuestions.question: Which gate numbers will the temporary modular building south of Dock B use when it opens (expected 2027), and which bus gates will close for the new Dock A works?
openQuestions.impact: Future status periods for bus gates cannot be dated yet.
openQuestions.howToResolve: Watch Flughafen Zürich newsroom / construction pages in 2027.

openQuestions.question: What is the official minimum connecting time at ZRH (Schengen/non-Schengen combinations)?
openQuestions.impact: Not used by the movement-only router, but useful as a rule. Only unofficial values (40 min, or 45–60 min) were found, and they contradict each other.
openQuestions.howToResolve: SWISS or Lufthansa Group connection-time page (Lufthansa business page returned HTTP 403 to automated access).
